triples.source_text: The Lord showed me this: Look, a brood of locusts was coming at dawn, and look, one bruchus locust, Gog the king.

target_units.text: What the caterpillar left, the locust devoured; what the locust left, the bruchus locust devoured; what the bruchus locust left, the blight devoured.

triples.relationship: locust and bruchus imagery in agricultural devastation
triples.rationale: Amos's vision presents a brood of locusts and a bruchus locust, followed in the next verse by devouring the land's grass. Joel likewise names locust and bruchus among successive devourers of what remains. This connection concerns the insects and their devastation, without identifying Amos's Gog label with another figure.

triples.source_text: When it finishes devouring the land’s grass, I said, “Lord, Lord, be merciful! Who will raise Jacob? He is so few!

target_units.text: In the midst of the altar’s platform the priests who minister to the Lord will weep and say, “Spare Thy people, Lord, and do not give Thine inheritance to reproach, for nations to rule over them, so that they do not say among the nations, ‘Where is their God?’”
Then the Lord became jealous for His land and spared His people.

triples.relationship: intercession for the people amid threatened devastation
triples.rationale: Amos pleads for mercy for Jacob, who is so few, as the locust vision reaches the land's grass. Joel's priests likewise ask the Lord to spare His people, followed by His sparing them. Both put an appeal for the people's preservation before the Lord.

triples.source_text: Relent, Lord, concerning this.” “This will not happen,” says the Lord.

target_units.text: Let not the Egyptians say, ‘He led them out with evil intent, to kill them in the mountains and consume them from the earth.’ Cease from Thy fierce anger and be merciful concerning Thy people’s evil,

remembering Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, Thy servants, to whom Thou didst swear by Thyself and speak, saying, ‘I will greatly multiply your seed as the stars of heaven in multitude’; and all this land which Thou didst say Thou wouldest give to their seed, they shall possess for ever.”
The Lord was appeased concerning the calamity He had said He would bring upon His people.

triples.relationship: appeal for mercy followed by withdrawal of announced calamity
triples.rationale: Amos's plea that the Lord relent is answered with the declaration that this will not happen. Moses likewise asks the Lord to cease from fierce anger and be merciful, after which the Lord is appeased concerning the calamity announced against His people.

triples.source_text: The Lord showed me this: Look, the Lord called for judgment by fire; it devoured the great abyss and devoured the portion.

target_units.text: For a fire has been kindled out of My wrath; it shall burn unto Hades beneath, devour the earth and its produce, and set ablaze the foundations of the mountains.

triples.relationship: divine judgment by fire reaching the depths and land
triples.rationale: Amos sees judgment by fire devouring the great abyss and the portion. Deuteronomy likewise describes fire kindled from divine wrath, burning to Hades beneath and devouring the earth and its produce. The connection is the fire's destructive reach, without equating the abyss with Hades.

triples.source_text: I said, “Lord, Lord, cease, please! Who will raise Jacob? He is so few!

target_units.text: When it finishes devouring the land’s grass, I said, “Lord, Lord, be merciful! Who will raise Jacob? He is so few!

triples.relationship: same-chapter repeated plea for Jacob's preservation
triples.rationale: Both appeals address the Lord and ask who will raise Jacob because he is so few. The first asks for mercy after the locust vision; the second asks Him to cease after the fire vision, repeating the reason for intercession.

triples.source_text: Relent, Lord, concerning this.” “This certainly will not happen,” says the Lord.

target_units.text: Relent, Lord, concerning this.” “This will not happen,” says the Lord.

triples.rationale: Both units follow a plea to relent with the Lord's declaration that the threatened event will not happen. The repeated answer links the locust and fire visions while preserving the second answer's emphatic wording.

triples.source_text: The Lord said to me, “What do you see, Amos?” I said, “Adamant.” The Lord said to me, “Look, I am setting adamant in the midst of My people Israel. I will certainly no longer pass them by,

target_units.text: He said, “What do you see, Amos?” I said, “A fowler’s vessel.” The Lord said to me, “The end has arrived upon My people Israel. I will certainly no longer pass them by.

triples.relationship: same-book vision question and repeated judgment refrain
triples.rationale: Both visions ask Amos what he sees, receive his answer naming the object, and end with the Lord declaring that He will no longer pass His people by. The objects remain distinct: adamant in chapter7 and a fowler's vessel in chapter8.

triples.source_text: and the altars of laughter will disappear, and Israel’s rites will be laid waste. I will rise against Jeroboam’s house with a sword.”

target_units.text: The shrines of On, Israel’s sins, will be removed; thorns and thistles will grow on their altars. They will say to the mountains, ‘Cover us!’ and to the hills, ‘Fall upon us!’

triples.relationship: judgment on Israel's altars and rites
triples.rationale: Amos announces that the altars of laughter will disappear and Israel's rites be laid waste. Hosea likewise announces removal of the shrines of On, described as Israel's sins, and thorns and thistles upon their altars. Both announce the ruin of places of worship without equating their different labels.

triples.source_text: Amaziah, priest of Bethel, sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, “Amos is forming conspiracies against you in the midst of Israel’s house. The land certainly cannot endure all his words,

target_units.text: And when Jeremiah stopped speaking everything the Lord commanded him to speak to all the people, the priests, false prophets, and all the people seized him, saying: You must die!
Because you prophesied in the Lord’s name, saying, This house will be like Shiloh and this city will be emptied of inhabitants. And all the people assembled against Jeremiah in the Lord’s house.
And Judah’s rulers heard this word and went up from the king’s house to the Lord’s house. They sat before the Lord’s New Gate.
And the priests and false prophets said to the rulers and all the people: A sentence of death for this man, because he prophesied against this city, as you heard with your own ears!

triples.relationship: religious officials accuse a prophet before political authorities
triples.rationale: Amaziah the priest reports Amos to Israel's king, alleging conspiracy and intolerable words. In Jeremiah, priests and false prophets likewise complain to the rulers about his prophecy against the city and demand death. Both accounts show opposition to a prophet's message being brought before governing authorities.

triples.source_text: because Amos says, ‘Jeroboam will die by a sword, and Israel will be led captive away from its land.’”

target_units.text: Therefore thus says the Lord: ‘Your wife will practice prostitution in the city, your sons and daughters will fall by a sword, and your land will be measured out with a cord. You will die in an unclean land, and Israel will be led captive away from its land.’”

triples.relationship: same-chapter recurrence of Israel's captivity prediction
triples.rationale: Amaziah's report attributes to Amos the prediction that Israel will be led captive away from its land. The later word addressed to Amaziah ends with that same prediction. This link concerns the captivity clause, without treating Amaziah's separate claim about Jeroboam's individual death as independently verified.

triples.source_text: Amaziah said to Amos, “Seer, go! Withdraw to Judah’s land; make your living there, and there you will prophesy.

target_units.text: At that very hour some Pharisees approached and said to Him, “Leave and go away from here, because Herod wants to kill Thee.”
And He said to them, “Go and tell that fox, ‘Behold, I drive out demons and accomplish healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I am brought to completion.’
Nevertheless, I must travel today and tomorrow and the day following, because it is not possible for a prophet to perish outside Jerusalem.

triples.relationship: pressure on a prophetic speaker to leave
triples.rationale: Amaziah tells Amos to withdraw to Judah, where he may make his living and prophesy. In Luke, Jesus is urged to leave because Herod wants to kill Him, and He answers in terms of a prophet's journey toward Jerusalem. Both passages place a demand to leave beside the prophetic mission, with different stated reasons.

triples.source_text: But you must never again prophesy at Bethel, because it is a king’s sanctuary and a house of kingship.”

target_units.text: They called them in and ordered them neither to speak nor to teach at all in the name of Jesus.
Peter and John answered them, “Judge whether it is right before God to listen to you rather than to God;
for we cannot keep from speaking about what we have seen and heard.”

triples.relationship: prohibition of public proclamation met by duty to God
triples.rationale: Amaziah prohibits Amos from prophesying at the royal sanctuary of Bethel. The council similarly prohibits Peter and John from speaking or teaching in Jesus' name, while they answer that they must speak what they have seen and heard. Amos's following reply likewise grounds his mission in the Lord's command.

triples.source_text: Amos answered Amaziah, “I was no prophet or prophet’s son, but a goat herder and one who scratches sycamore figs,

target_units.text: On that day the prophets will be ashamed, each because of his vision when he prophesies; they will wear a hairy skin because they lied.
He will say, ‘I am no prophet; I am a man who works the earth, because a man begot me from my youth.’

triples.relationship: contrasting uses of a denial of prophetic status and an agricultural occupation
triples.rationale: Amos says he was no prophet or prophet's son but a goat herder and sycamore-fig worker, before recounting the Lord's call. Zechariah's speaker likewise denies being a prophet and names work on the earth, in a context of prophets ashamed of lying. The verbal pattern is shared while the contexts and purposes differ.

triples.source_text: and the Lord took me from the sheep, and the Lord said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to My people Israel.’

target_units.text: Now say this to My servant David: Thus says the Lord Almighty: I took you from the sheepfold to be ruler over My people, over Israel,

triples.relationship: the Lord takes a person from tending sheep to service over Israel
triples.rationale: Amos says the Lord took him from the sheep and commanded him to prophesy to His people Israel. The word to David likewise recalls the Lord taking him from the sheepfold to be ruler over Israel. The call from the flock is shared, while prophecy and kingship remain distinct tasks.

triples.source_text: Now hear the Lord’s word: You say, ‘Do not prophesy against Israel, and you must not stir up a crowd against Jacob’s house.’

target_units.text: For this is a disobedient people, lying sons who did not want to hear God’s law,
who say to the prophets, “Do not announce to us,” and to those seeing visions, “Do not speak to us. Instead, speak to us and announce another deception,
and turn us from this way, remove this path from us, and remove Israel’s Holy One from us.”

triples.rationale: Amos repeats the prohibition on prophesying against Israel and stirring up a crowd against Jacob's house. Isaiah likewise describes a disobedient people telling prophets and visionaries not to announce or speak, asking instead for deception. Both passages report attempts to suppress unwelcome prophetic speech.
